tagline: Up a sand spit between ocean and bay, then over.
intro: From Imperial Beach the highway curves north onto the Silver Strand, a low, narrow isthmus of sand seven miles long with the Pacific on one side and San Diego Bay on the other. It passes Navy training beaches and Silver Strand State Beach, crosses the Naval Amphibious Base and comes into Coronado as Orange Avenue, the main street. From there it climbs onto the bridge.

The strand road opened in 1924 with a festival at Tent City, Coronado's summer resort. After a highway project around 1939 the route ran through Tent City itself and, by the account of a later city works director, contributed to its demise.

moments.title: Silver Strand
moments.text: On the ocean side, two and a half miles of shoreline are trimmed with silver shells, which is how the strand got its name.

moments.title: Coronado
moments.text: Orange Avenue runs through a town that keeps the Hotel del Coronado, a wooden Victorian beach resort that was the largest resort hotel in the world when it opened in 1888.

moments.title: San Diego-Coronado Bridge
moments.text: It rises from Coronado at a 4.67 percent grade and swings 80 degrees toward San Diego, a curve that lengthens the bridge to give Navy ships 200 feet of clearance.
